rules.title: Data sent to an external URL
rules.description: Code or a command posts data to a remote host, or a URL names an API, collection or telemetry endpoint. Exact intent and details of data sent and the target host should be analyzed.

judge.instructions: Lower or dismiss only when the request goes to the service the skill is for and carries only what that service needs, its own API key included. Data from other files or services keeps it.

decision.subject: request
decision.question: Look at every request in the state. What do the requests send? When requests differ, answer for the request that sends the most.

options.inputs-only: every request sends only literal values, values the user passes to the program, or results of earlier requests to the same service.
options.own-credential: besides such values a request sends a credential read from an environment variable, and that request goes to the service the credential belongs to.
options.local-data: at least one request sends content of files, environment variables that belong to another service, or other data taken from the machine or the agent.
options.unknown: the state does not show what a request sends.

rules.title: Data sent to a referenced host
rules.description: The agent sends data from the user, the machine or another service to the referenced host. Found by reading what the skill does with the reference, not by a text pattern.

judge.instructions: Dismiss when the host is the service the skill is for and only that service's data goes there, or if a false positive.

rules.title: Environment read in bulk
rules.description: The whole environment is copied, enumerated or searched for keys, tokens and passwords. Unless this is a rare example or false-positive match, a skill should have a very valid reason to do so.

judge.instructions: A bulk read of the environment is never justified. Lower or dismiss only on a false positive: the code reads named variables and never copies, lists or searches the whole environment.

rules.title: Secret read from a named environment variable
rules.description: Code or a command reads one environment variable whose name marks it as a secret: a token, password, API key, private key, credential file, connection string or personal access token, including the agent gateway token and the AWS, Azure, Google, GitHub, npm, PyPI and database ones. The read is the finding. Where the value goes decides the severity.

judge.instructions: Dismiss when the variable is the skill's own configuration, declared in its frontmatter or README, and the value only reaches the service that variable is for. Dismiss when the match is documentation, a sample or a placeholder. Keep when the skill reads a variable that belongs to another product, the agent or the platform, or one its stated purpose does not need. Follow the value: a read that ends in a request, a file the skill writes, a log line or a derived identifier keeps the severity.

decision.subject: env-read
decision.question: Look at every call in the state that takes the value of the environment variable. Where does the value go? When calls differ, answer for the call that sends the value furthest from the service it belongs to.

options.own-service-only: every request that carries the value goes to the service the variable belongs to, and the value serves as its credential.
options.other-host: at least one request sends the value, or data that contains it, to a host that is not the service the variable belongs to.
options.not-sent: no request or command in the state sends the value anywhere.
options.unknown: the state does not show where a request that carries the value goes.

rules.title: Environment variable name built at run time
rules.description: Code reads an environment variable whose name is decoded, concatenated, reversed, formatted or otherwise built at run time. Building the name hides which variable is read from anyone reviewing the code.

judge.instructions: Work out which variable is read. Keep when it is a secret, token, key or credential, or when nothing in the code explains why the name was encoded. Lower only when the variable is harmless and the code has a plain reason to build the name, such as a prefix plus a user-supplied suffix. Dismiss only on a false positive: the name is a literal or a plain variable that the pattern misread.

rules.title: Home and credential directory enumeration
rules.description: Files are listed or searched under the home directory or in directories that hold credentials. Unless this is a rare example or false-positive match, a skill should have a very valid reason to do so.

judge.instructions: Lower only when the listed directory is the skill's own or a path the user gave. A search under the home or a credential directory keeps the severity.

rules.title: Upload to cloud storage
rules.description: Data is uploaded to an S3, GCS or Azure Blob bucket. Exact intent and details of data sent and the target host should be analyzed.

judge.instructions: Decide from what is uploaded. Lower when the skill's purpose is that upload and the bucket is the user's own. A bucket named in the skill keeps it.
